The comparison of which firm makes the most extensive or strongest claims about AI in advice delivery cannot be made on a single shared quantitative basis, because the firms report different metrics across different scopes and periods: Bank of America cites company-wide figures of 200,000+ teammates using AI tools and 300-plus approved use cases, while Schwab cites 33,000 employees equipped with AI tools and more than 220 use cases firm-wide, Raymond James cites roughly $1 billion/$1.1 billion of technology (including AI) spend and 10,000 associates using AI, and Morgan Stanley makes qualitative priority claims (overweight then double overweight to AI, top priority, existentially important) rather than a single comparable count. For these reasons a single ranking is not valid. On the strength of rhetoric alone, the strongest qualitative claims are Morgan Stanley's (calling AI existentially important and the top priority for the firm as the adviser) and Schwab's (describing itself as already an AI-enabled company, calling AI an enormous accelerant, and stating no one can match its combination of AI and people).
